chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukayr, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:
The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) liked the arm (of the sheep).
ai.seo_question: What part of the sheep did the Prophet Muhammad prefer?
ai.summary: This brief hadith from al-Kafi records the Prophet Muhammad’s (peace be upon him) preference for the arm (al-dhirā') of the sheep, reflecting the Sunnah of selecting the best portions for distribution. In Shia scholarly tradition, this is often interpreted not merely as a culinary preference but as a demonstration of the Prophet’s discernment in choosing the most tender and esteemed cuts, thereby establishing a normative practice for charitable distribution and family meals.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukeyr, from Zurara, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘The arm (of the sheep) was liked by Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>’.
en.sarwar: 2. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn Faddal from ibn Bukayr from Zurarah who has said the following: “Abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that
the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, liked shoulder meat greatly.’”
